request.user:
Subject: Zoology
Question type: single-correct (exactly one option is right)

Aggregates of lymphoid tissue present in the distal portion of the small intestine are known as
(A) Villi
(B) Peyer’s patches
(C) Rugae
(D) Choroid plexux

result.working: Peyer's patches are aggregated lymphoid follicles (part of MALT/GALT) in the mucosa and submucosa of the ileum, the distal part of the small intestine. Villi are finger-like absorptive projections, not lymphoid tissue. Rugae are folds of the stomach mucosa. The choroid plexus lies in the brain ventricles and produces CSF.
result.note: Option D is misspelt 'Choroid plexux'; it should read 'Choroid plexus'. This does not affect the answer.
